title: Change the priority of a running process
summary: Adjust how much CPU time a specific running process gets. Lower niceness values give the process more CPU time, while higher values give it less.

steps.explain: Run renice with the -n flag to set the new niceness value and -p to specify the process ID. A value of -20 is highest priority, 19 is lowest.

placeholders.name: NICENESS_VALUE
placeholders.description: The new priority level, from -20 (highest) to 19 (lowest).

placeholders.name: PROCESS_ID
placeholders.description: The ID of the process to modify.

rollback.explain: To revert the change, run renice again with the original niceness value (usually 0 for normal priority).

warnings: Changing priority to a very low value (negative) can make the system unresponsive if the process consumes all CPU.
You may need root privileges to change the priority of processes owned by other users.
